title: DepthGraft: Structural Regularization through Hierarchical Cross-Layer KV Reconstruction
summary: DepthGraft replaces standard per-layer KV computation (and prior adjacent/global-anchor KV sharing) with a pretraining-time architecture where deep-layer KV is reconstructed from stride-aligned shallow-middle source pairs. It costs a full pretraining run under a modified architecture, adds cross-layer reconstruction logic to the model definition, and yields only about one-third KV cache reduction at inference. It can fail because all results are pretraining-based on 0.5B-16B models, so the method cannot be retrofitted to existing checkpoints, the reported gains may not transfer to other data mixes or scales, and third-party implementations of an unverified arXiv architecture may diverge.
rationale: The technique requires training models from scratch under a custom architecture, which exceeds the reader's infrastructure and rules out adoption on existing models, so it is only worth monitoring until pretrained checkpoints or independent validation appear.

claims.statement: DepthGraft replaces standard per-layer KV computation (and prior adjacent/global-anchor KV sharing) with a pretraining-time architecture where deep-layer KV is reconstructed from stride-aligned shallow-middle source pairs. It costs a full pretraining run under a modified architecture, adds cross-layer reconstruction logic to the model definition, and yields only about one-third KV cache reduction at inference. It can fail because all results are pretraining-based on 0.5B-16B models, so the method cannot be retrofitted to existing checkpoints, the reported gains may not transfer to other data mixes or scales, and third-party implementations of an unverified arXiv architecture may diverge.

On a 16B MoE model, DepthGraft reports +7.0 absolute points on MMLU-Pro, +6.6 on CMMLU, and +6.4 on C3, with roughly one-third KV cache reduction; gains are accuracy points, not a multiplicative factor.
